text.p: French aluminium and packaging giant Pechiney predicted on Thursday that provisions for the "Challenge" cost-cutting plan would push the group in the red in 1996.
Chairman Jean-Pierre Rodier told a news conference that provisions for the two billion francs ($388.9 million) restructuring plan would result in a loss for the year.
First half net income fell to 426 million francs in the first half of 1996 from 658 million francs in the same period for 1995.
The company predicted earlier 1996 earnings would drop, citing the absence of signs of an economic recovery in Europe and volatile aluminium prices.

"Based on current information, the Group believes that net earnings for the full year 1996, before taking into account the costs related to the Challenge project, will not reach the level of 1995 earnings on a pro forma basis (i.e. 732 million francs)", it said in a statement released ahead of the news conference.
The Challenge plan seeks to find four bilion francs in cost savings by the end of 1998.
Along with these savings, investments of about 3.5 billion francs will be made over the next three years.
In the first half of 1996, Pechiney faced a worldwide reduction in demand from primary aluminium stemming from a sluggish European economy.
But it benefited from lower financial expenses resulting from asset sales completed in 1995 and a capital boost that came along with its privatisation.

First half operating profit fell to 1.47 billion francs from 1.98 billion. Two-thirds of the decline came from the International Trade which had a strong performance in the first half 1995 and to changes in accounting for the Components and Systems division from consolidation to equity basis.
Weak demand and lower prices drove aluminium sales down 9.7 percent and operating profit down 17 percent.

In the packaging division sales rose 2.7 percent but profit was down 12 percent. Sales volume increased in Europe but declined slightly in the United States. Results for the North American operations were hurt by competitive pressure on prices.

In the Food, Healthcare and Beauty division, flexible packaging in the United States and the plastic tube business in Europe had a strong performance. But other activities, mostly in Europe had a stable to weaker performance.
The gearing ratio at end June 1996 was 89 percent against 85 percent at end December 1995.
Pechiney shares closed 0.70 francs lower at 213.30 francs before the profit figures and forecast was announced. ($ = 5.143 French Francs)
